{{recipesummary|category=Recipes for dessert|servings=8|time=1 hour|difficulty=3}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|Cuisine of France]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (see notes)
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 5 [[Cookbook:Apple|Golden Delicious apples]], peeled, cored and quartered
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pastry Dough (recipe)|pastry dough recipe]]

==Procedure==

# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven_temperatures|400°F]].
# Place sugar, butter and water in a stovetop/oven-safe [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|tarte dish]] over medium-high heat. Cook until mixture becomes golden brown and bubbly.
# Remove from heat and allow mixture to cool to room temperature in the tarte dish.
# When caramel mixture has cooled, arrange the apple quarters on their sides in the mixture.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] the pastry dough out to a thickness of about ½ inch and a diameter large enough to cover the tarte dish.
# Place dough on top of the tarte, then trim and discard the edges.
# [[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] tarte for 40 minutes.
# Allow to cool in the tarte dish for 15 minutes before inverting onto a serving platter.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* European-style butter, which has a higher fat content than American butter, is recommended. Most US supermarkets now stock at least one variety of European-style butter, Plugra being one of the most popular brands.
